Q11: Apply Resolution method to prove a theorem
Resolution is a rule of inference used to derive new clauses by eliminating complementary  literals, ultimately proving
Steps:
1. Convert all statements to CNF (Conjunctive Normal Form)  2. Negate the goal/theorem to be proved  3. Add negated goal
Worked Example:
Prove: Socrates is mortal
Given Premises:
1. All humans are mortal → ∀x Human(x) → Mortal(x)  2. Socrates is human → Human(Socrates)
Step 1 — Convert to CNF:
Clause  Statement  Source
C1  ¬Human(x) ∨ Mortal(x)  Premise 1 (eliminate implication)
C2  Human(Socrates)  Premise 2
C3  ¬Mortal(Socrates)  Negated Goal
Step 2 — Apply Resolution:
C1: ¬Human(x) ∨ Mortal(x)
C3: ¬Mortal(Socrates)
───────────────────────────── Resolve on Mortal, unify x = Socrates
C4: ¬Human(Socrates)
C2: Human(Socrates)
C4: ¬Human(Socrates)
───────────────────────────── Resolve on Human(Socrates)
C5: □ (Empty Clause)
Conclusion: Empty clause derived → contradiction found → Mortal(Socrates) is proved ✓
